lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: copying segments and angles

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle. Central angle per side?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the perpendicular bisector construction?
choices: Any line through the midpoint is a perpendicular bisector.
The arcs look symmetric, so the line must be perpendicular.
Both constructed points are equidistant from the endpoints, and the locus of such points is exactly the perpendicular bisector.
The compass width was more than half the segment, which forces perpendicularity.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a angle?
choices: the amount of turn measured in degrees
the space between two intersecting lines
the figure formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint
a corner of a polygon

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. With the compass set to the radius, mark successive arcs around the circle from a starting point, then join consecutive marks. What has been constructed?
choices: a square inscribed in the circle
a regular hexagon inscribed in the circle
an equilateral triangle inscribed in the circle
a regular pentagon inscribed in the circle

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 5. What central angle does each side subtend?
Which statement correctly justifies the angle bisector construction?
choices: The construction relies on the angle being acute.
The construction builds two congruent triangles by SSS, so the angles at the vertex are congruent.
Equal arcs always produce equal angles regardless of the triangle.
The ray drawn appears to split the angle evenly.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a perpendicular lines?
choices: two lines that intersect to form right angles
two lines that form an isosceles triangle
two lines that never meet
two lines with opposite slopes

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. From vertex V draw an arc crossing both rays at P and Q. From P and Q draw equal arcs meeting at R. Draw ray VR. What has been constructed?
choices: the bisector of the angle at V
an equilateral triangle on PQ
the perpendicular bisector of PQ only
a line perpendicular to one ray

items.prompt: A regular hexagon is inscribed in a circle of radius 8. What central angle does each side subtend?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: Which statement correctly justifies the equilateral triangle construction on a given segment?
choices: The circles intersect, which guarantees 60° angles by definition.
Both circles have radius equal to the segment, so all three sides are that same length.
The intersection point is the midpoint of the segment.
The construction works only when the segment is horizontal.

items.prompt: Which statement is a precise definition of a parallel lines?
choices: two lines the same distance apart at one point
two coplanar lines that never intersect, however far they are extended
two lines with the same length
two lines that meet only at infinity

items.prompt: A construction proceeds as follows. Through point P not on line ℓ, copy the angle that a transversal makes with ℓ, placing the copy at P on the same transversal. What has been constructed?
choices: a line through P perpendicular to ℓ
the reflection of ℓ across P
the perpendicular bisector of the transversal
a line through P parallel to ℓ
